subject: Hospitality
title: Mise en Place: Everything in Its Place
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mise en Place: Everything in Its Place.

hook.text: 'Mise en place' is the French term for having everything prepped, measured, and organized before cooking begins.

buildup.text: Vegetables chopped, sauces ready, stations clean. Professional kitchens spend hours on prep before a single order comes in.

discovery.text: Mise en place isn't just physical—it's mental. Top chefs say it's a philosophy: prepare thoroughly, execute calmly.

twist.text: During service, there's no time to prep. If your mise en place is wrong, you'll fall behind and never catch up.

climax.text: Business schools now teach mise en place as a productivity principle. Prepare everything before you start any complex task.

punchline.text: Prep before you cook. A kitchen principle that works everywhere.

quiz.question: What does 'mise en place' mean?
options: Everything in its place—prepped and organized before cooking
